one_line: Privacy-first support navigator pairing human-controlled facts with auditable agent actions.
what_it_does: Exposes structured tools for discovering support options, analyzing a case, explaining and comparing options, loading demo cases, and preparing next steps while keeping facts and rule-engine results visible.
leverage_rationale: Typed support-domain tools and shared deterministic state materially outperform brittle scraping for rule-heavy, sensitive workflows, though the demonstrated domain remains a bounded navigator.
leverage_evidence: About text describes six structured tools and a shared deterministic JavaScript rule engine.
Frame sequence shows a structured support workflow moving from controls to agent activity and updated result records.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent workflow and visible updated states, but lacks transcript and fine-grained end-to-end proof of every support operation.
execution_evidence: Three submitted video frame sheets show initial UI, operational/agent state, and resulting structured records.
Public repository and live demo are reported in packet facts.
impact_rationale: People navigating complex public-service or support eligibility rules have a concrete need for understandable, auditable assistance without surrendering sensitive facts.
impact_evidence: Description identifies rule-heavy support and public-service sites as the target problem.
Human retains control of facts and eligibility is not delegated to the agent.
creativity_rationale: The human-controls-facts/agent-orchestrates model is a thoughtful application of WebMCP to a sensitive support workflow.
creativity_evidence: Privacy-first support navigator with visible matched and missing conditions.
Auditable activity log and shared rule engine are pursued as core interaction design.
usability_note: Structured, reviewable workflow appears usable for complex support cases.
red_flags: No transcript; some frame text is small.
standouts: Strong human/agent boundary for sensitive facts.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and credible public-service value with visible product-motion evidence.

one_line: Turns any passage into a shared, personalized language-learning workspace.
what_it_does: Learners and agents annotate text, create grammar missions and review activities, generate passages, leave feedback, and maintain vocabulary and learning context in one interface.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent precise access to lesson context and lets it make visible, undoable changes directly in the reading workspace; a general agent could approximate this with more friction.
leverage_evidence: Description lists six tools for context, annotations, missions, activities, feedback, and passage generation.
Frames show document cards and expanded annotation/action states followed by updated lesson content.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent from text/lesson setup through agent edits and visible learning artifacts, with a polished scope for a hackathon project.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show a reading-oriented UI, agent-expanded controls, and populated/updated annotated content.
Description states every agent action creates a visible change and can be undone for passage replacement.
impact_rationale: Language learners have a clear recurring need for contextual explanations, practice, and retention; the integrated workspace directly addresses fragmentation.
impact_evidence: Description identifies the copy-to-chat/manual-saving problem.
Features cover contextual annotations, exercises, review, and export.
creativity_rationale: The margin-based collaboration model and hidden-answer grammar missions are a fresh synthesis beyond generic translation chat.
creativity_evidence: Learner and agent share the same reading workspace.
Agent can add selective annotations and create contextual missions without taking over the learning process.
usability_note: Focused reading plus inline annotations and practice should reduce context switching.
red_flags: Video text is partly illegible at contact-sheet scale.
standouts: Visible, reversible agent edits in context.
advance_reason: Well-integrated education workflow with strong evidence and differentiated interaction model.

one_line: A shared evidence workspace where humans and agents build and verify versioned cases.
what_it_does: Maintains claims, evidence, provenance, conflicts, deterministic evaluations, and audit lineage through narrow structured tools and a governed case state.
leverage_rationale: The product's central value is shared structured state, provenance, revision binding, and decision lineage that a general UI-driving agent would struggle to maintain reliably.
leverage_evidence: Description enumerates tools for reading cases, revising claims, adding evidence, identifying conflicts, evaluating, and exporting.
Frames show a structured evidence workspace progressing through populated and resolved verification cards.
execution_rationale: The evidence/case workflow appears coherent and intentionally governed, though the lack of transcript limits certainty about full completion.
execution_evidence: Video frames show dark evidence cards across initial, expanded, and updated states.
Description specifies versioned cases, deterministic verdicts, and exportable audit lineage.
impact_rationale: Researchers, journalists, analysts, and other web investigators benefit from preserving provenance and challenging claims instead of relying on opaque agent conclusions.
impact_evidence: Problem statement centers on shared state, provenance, uncertainty, and decision lineage.
Inbound and outbound distillation protocols are described as governance boundaries.
creativity_rationale: The governed case and two-way distillation protocol are an ambitious, memorable interaction model for accountable web intelligence.
creativity_evidence: Human and agent operate on the same versioned case rather than parallel hidden context.
Conflict identification and explicit source roles are core product concepts.
usability_note: Structured evidence cards support review, but the governance model may be cognitively demanding.
red_flags: Demo availability is unknown in packet facts.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP rationale and high-value research/investigative use case.

one_line: Grants agents narrow, temporary authority without giving them reusable human credentials.
what_it_does: Separates human authentication from agent authorization through scoped requests, one-time approval, single-use commits, and audit receipts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used as the controlled capability boundary: the page can expose narrowly scoped actions and require human approval without handing the agent a broad session or credential.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly contrasts temporary agent authority with passwords, API keys, OAuth tokens, and authenticated sessions.
Frame sequence shows authority-request/approval UI and a resulting scoped authorization/audit state.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent security flow from request through approval, commit, consumption, and receipt, with substantial visual evidence.
execution_evidence: Eight named gallery concepts cover browser verification, email verification, address authority, approval, commit, consumption, and audit receipt.
Three video sheets show administrative panels, approval dialogs, and updated authority state.
impact_rationale: Credential over-privilege is a real barrier to safe agent action; scoped, revocable authority has broad value for users and application builders.
impact_evidence: Description targets real actions such as changing addresses without exposing credentials.
Design principle is explicit: humans authenticate, agents receive only task-specific authority.
creativity_rationale: The separation of identity from temporary agent authority is a strong and memorable security interaction model pursued through a complete lifecycle.
creativity_evidence: Single-use authority and consumed audit receipts are concrete extensions beyond generic approval dialogs.
The product treats the agent as an authority requester rather than another logged-in user.
usability_note: Explicit approval and constrained authority favor user trust, though security flows add steps.
red_flags: No transcript; some technical UI details are small.
standouts: Strongest security thesis in the packet.
advance_reason: High-impact, WebMCP-native authorization model with unusually strong scope and evidence.

one_line: An agent-assisted calendar that finds time and manages events from natural-language goals.
what_it_does: Reads schedules, finds available time, creates and manages events, and handles recurring calendars and conflicts through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Structured calendar state makes multi-event scheduling more reliable than manual UI driving, but general agents and existing calendar APIs can achieve much of the outcome.
leverage_evidence: Description gives the concrete workflow of finding multiple study blocks around existing classes.
Frames show calendar/workspace states, an operational dialog, and updated schedule/data panels.
execution_rationale: The central calendar concept and agent-edit flow appear functional, with likely minor gaps around the broad claims of conflict and recurring-event handling.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show an initial workspace, agent operation, and changed records.
Public repository and live demo are reported in packet facts.
impact_rationale: Students and busy people have a concrete scheduling burden, and goal-based time placement can save meaningful effort.
impact_evidence: Description is grounded in classes, sports, music, work, and reshuffling constraints.
Calendar supports finding time rather than merely storing events.
creativity_rationale: Agent-driven calendar planning is a useful but familiar category, with novelty mainly in the WebMCP shared-calendar interaction.
creativity_evidence: Natural-language goal to scheduled blocks is clearly demonstrated as the concept.
Multiple calendars and conflict handling add scope but are not wholly novel.
usability_note: Goal-based scheduling can reduce manual calendar manipulation.
red_flags: Broad feature claims exceed what can be verified from small frame sheets.
standouts: Good fit for structured state manipulation.
advance_reason: Credible productivity value and visible workflow, though leverage and creativity are moderate.

one_line: A role-aware agent embedded in operational systems for booking and schedule management.
what_it_does: Lets customers and owners use natural language to book visits, inspect availability, stage conflict-free plans, approve exact revisions, and share the same live data.
leverage_rationale: Role- and state-aware WebMCP tools, one-shot approvals, state-hash binding, and atomic procedures make consequential operational changes safer and more reliable than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description details customer/owner shared state, exact approval, row-level security, plan hashes, and atomic database procedures.
Frames show a green operational interface, expanded agent workflow, and consolidated updated booking state.
execution_rationale: The booking scenario is concrete and the packet describes concurrency handling, approvals, email delivery, and isolated sandboxes; frames show the workflow changing state.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show initial cards, intermediate agent/action panels, and resulting booking/status layout.
Description gives a detailed customer booking and owner conflict-resolution sequence.
impact_rationale: Small businesses with fragmented booking/CRM/ERP dashboards can gain substantial value from conversational operations with human confirmation.
impact_evidence: Target users are owners drowning in dashboards and customers making bookings.
Demo includes availability, conflict handling, and customer notification.
creativity_rationale: The two-sided customer/owner workflow and cryptographically bound one-shot approval show deeper operational design than a generic chat wrapper.
creativity_evidence: Same data is read by website, workspace, and agent.
State-hash approval aborts stale plans and preserves exact human intent.
usability_note: Natural-language operations plus exact approval reduce dashboard burden while preserving control.
advance_reason: Excellent operational WebMCP use with credible execution and meaningful business value.

one_line: A shared-browser marketplace for buying and selling agent-ready data with explicit terms and approval.
what_it_does: Publishes structured samples, exposes source/license/price details, negotiates a deterministic proposal, obtains human approval, delivers usable rows and manifests, and supports undo.
leverage_rationale: The agent can discover structured listings, negotiate under deterministic rules, and commit against shared balances and delivery state; this is substantially beyond scraping a marketplace UI.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies structured samples, visible license and price terms, exact approval, balance changes, row delivery, and undo.
Frames show a dashboard/data exchange flow progressing to populated transaction and record panels.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete two-sided transaction lifecycle and the video frames show product states changing through it.
execution_evidence: Concrete synthetic Sydney dataset scenario includes discovery, counteroffer, approval, commit, delivery, and undo.
Three video sheets show initial dashboard, expanded exchange/data views, and resulting records.
impact_rationale: Small operators, data contributors, and agent builders have a real need for usable, licensed data handoffs, though the demonstrated marketplace is intentionally narrow.
impact_evidence: Description names small business owners, independent contributors, and agent builders.
Delivered rows include source/license manifest and can be consumed directly by an agent.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-human and human-to-agent data commerce with deterministic negotiation, exact approval, and reversible delivery is highly original and ambitious.
creativity_evidence: Two-sided shared-browser marketplace is the central concept.
Undo restores balances and blocks further delivery, extending the transaction model beyond a simple listing.
usability_note: Explicit terms and sample delivery support trust, while marketplace workflows are more involved than ordinary browsing.
red_flags: Synthetic data and credits limit evidence of real-world marketplace readiness.
advance_reason: Highly original WebMCP-native transaction workflow with strong demonstrated state handling.

one_line: An NBA salary-cap co-pilot that repairs failed multi-team trades under CBA constraints.
what_it_does: Provides a 30-team trade canvas and constraint solver that turns salary-cap violations into compliant trade adjustments for fans, journalists, and analysts.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to complex trade state and automated constraint solving can replace extensive manual calculation and repeated UI edits, though the concept could be built with other APIs.
leverage_evidence: Description details piecewise salary brackets, aprons, TPEs, roster limits, and autonomous repair suggestions.
Frames show a dense planning canvas, tool/dialog stage, and updated result cards/data blocks.
execution_rationale: The product has a clear, ambitious domain workflow with a visible interactive canvas and computed outcomes; factual legal compliance is claimed more strongly than independently demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show a structured trade workspace and changed calculation/result states.
Description specifies a 30-team canvas, constraint solver, and WebMCP tool surfaces.
impact_rationale: NBA fans, journalists, podcasters, and analysts have a strong interest in testing complex trades, and fixing dead-end errors is genuinely useful for that audience.
impact_evidence: Description identifies the audience and the manual 29-tab/45-minute calculation burden.
Product addresses failed trades with actionable solutions rather than only rejection.
creativity_rationale: Turning a trade machine into a repair-oriented human/AI co-pilot is a fresh interaction model for a specialized rules domain.
creativity_evidence: Core promise is 'here is how we fix it' rather than simply pass/fail.
Multi-team routing and CBA constraint explanation add meaningful ambition.
usability_note: Visual canvas and actionable repairs could make a difficult rules domain approachable, though density may challenge novices.
red_flags: Legally compliant/CBA claims are not independently verifiable from packet evidence.
Category is specialized and the frame text is small.
standouts: Solver repairs failures instead of only reporting them.
advance_reason: High-value specialized co-pilot with clear novelty and strong product evidence.

one_line: An agent-native search-and-rescue incident board where the commander approves the plan.
what_it_does: Shares live search segments, team availability, coverage, probability, and staged plans between an agent and incident commander while forbidding direct team dispatch.
leverage_rationale: The agent needs precise shared operational state and recomputation of search theory while the human retains dispatch authority; generic UI driving is materially less reliable and auditable.
leverage_evidence: Description centers on live board state, typed tools, immediate rendering, and agent replanning after human intervention.
Frames show a board/grid interface moving through denser planning state to updated forms/cards and layout.
execution_rationale: The scope is focused and the packet describes a coherent briefing-to-staged-plan workflow with a deliberate safety boundary; full field use is not demonstrated.
execution_evidence: Video sheets show a board-like initial UI, agent planning state, and changed board/result state.
Description specifies probability-of-area, probability-of-detection, expected gain, team assignments, and staged approval.
impact_rationale: Search-and-rescue commanders and volunteers face time-critical coordination with real human consequences; better prioritization and shared state can directly improve decisions.
impact_evidence: Description identifies wilderness search constraints: fading daylight, weather, radio load, teams, and probability maps.
Human commander decides and there is explicitly no dispatch tool.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a safety-bounded search-theory command board is unusually ambitious, memorable, and deeply aligned with human/agent complementarity.
creativity_evidence: Agent plans while commander decides is embedded in the interaction model.
The no-dispatch-tool constraint is a meaningful governance design, not a disclaimer.
usability_note: A focused board could help under pressure, but operational complexity and training requirements are significant.
red_flags: High-stakes deployment readiness is not established by a hackathon packet.
Primary category is a difficult taxonomy fit; other is used because no emergency-response category exists.
advance_reason: Transformative shared-state use case with unusually strong impact and creativity.

one_line: An agent-guided coding classroom where learners practice inside the lesson workspace.
what_it_does: Uses WebMCP tools to prepare lessons, configure examples, explain HTML/CSS/JavaScript concepts, highlight code, and validate learner exercises.
leverage_rationale: The agent can configure and update the instructional workspace directly, linking explanations, code highlighting, and exercises more reliably than a separate chat window, though the learning outcome is also possible with other integrations.
leverage_evidence: Description says the agent creates a learning plan, examples, visual explanations, and practice exercises through structured tools.
Frames show instructional/editor panels, an agent-guided intermediate state, and updated lesson or validation content.
execution_rationale: The packet demonstrates a coherent classroom loop from connection and lesson setup through explanation, practice, and feedback, with polished scope.
execution_evidence: Gallery descriptions enumerate setup, explanation, learner exercise, validation, and code highlighting states.
Video sheets show an educational workspace progressing to updated editor/result panels.
impact_rationale: Beginning programmers have a clear need for connected explanations, concrete examples, and immediate low-stakes practice.
impact_evidence: Description is grounded in the confusion of learning programming and fragmented guidance.
Learner, rather than agent, completes exercises and receives validation feedback.
creativity_rationale: The integrated agent classroom and practice-first teaching loop are a fresh synthesis, though coding tutors are an established category.
creativity_evidence: The agent prepares a structured classroom rather than only answering questions.
Explanations connect highlighted code to learner practice in the same workspace.
usability_note: Focused lessons and immediate practice should reduce context switching for beginners.
red_flags: No transcript; broad curriculum depth is not established.
standouts: Strong pedagogical division of labor: agent guides, learner practices.
Visible connection between explanation and code.
advance_reason: Coherent educational workflow with credible audience value and visible end-to-end progression.
